Avatars.doc:
One account's avatars, keyed by device (see `caller`). The slot belongs to
the account, and so does the map nested in it: every node refuses another
account's write to either, so nobody can move, rename or evict someone
else's avatar, or squat a device id before its owner first joins.

fields.name: devices
fields.doc: Device identity (64 hex) -> that device's player row.

BlockOverride.doc: A stored block edit: block id `b` and the stamp that orders concurrent edits.

fields.name: b
fields.doc: Block id, 0 to 15; 0 is air (a broken block).

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.doc: Room-clock unix seconds; the larger stamp wins when two players edit one block.

Edit.doc: One block change at a world coordinate.

fields.name: y
fields.doc: World y, in [0, 64); y is up.

fields.name: b
fields.doc: Block id: 0 air, 1 grass, 2 dirt, 3 stone, 4 sand, 5 water, 6 wood, 7 leaves, 8 plank, 9 glass, 10 brick, 11 torch, 12 glowstone, 13 bedrock, 14 cobble, 15 snow.

MeroBlocks.doc: One world: its fixed metadata, every block edit and every account's players.

fields.name: meta
fields.doc:
name + seed + day-clock anchor. Every client derives the terrain from
the seed, so changing it after creation would rebuild the world under
everyone's edits: frozen, nobody (the creator included) can.

fields.name: overrides
fields.doc:
"x,y,z" -> override. Set-only (break = b:0), never removed. Public on
purpose: the world is collaborative.

fields.name: players
fields.doc: Each account's avatars, writable only by that account.

Player.doc: A player row: presence and last known transform, keyed by the player's device identity.

fields.name: y
fields.doc: Position in blocks; y is up.

fields.name: sel
fields.doc: Selected hotbar slot, 0 to 8; peers render what the player holds.

fields.name: left
fields.doc: Whether the player has left; set by `leave`, cleared by `join` or `heartbeat`.

PlayerView.doc: A player as other players see them.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The player's context identity (device key, 64 hex).

fields.name: y
fields.doc: Position in blocks; y is up.

fields.name: sel
fields.doc: Selected hotbar slot, 0 to 8; peers render what the player holds.

fields.name: online
fields.doc: Not left, and heard from within the last 10 s.

fields.name: y
fields.doc: Position in blocks; y is up.

WorldMeta.doc: The world's identity: name, terrain seed and creation time. Fixed at creation.

fields.name: seed
fields.doc: Terrain seed; clients generate identical terrain from it.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.doc: Unix seconds; the 600 s day/night cycle is counted from here.

methods.name: get_overrides
methods.doc:
Every edited coordinate as `{"k": "x,y,z", "b": <block id>}`.

A key never disappears: a broken block stays listed with `b: 0`. Any
coordinate not listed holds generated terrain.

# Examples
```json
{}
```
methods.returns_doc: Every edited coordinate as `{"k": "x,y,z", "b": <block id>}`, breaks included.

methods.name: get_players
methods.doc:
Every player row with an `online` flag.

A player is online when they have not left and wrote within the last 10 s,
measured against the newest clock any player has reported (at most 15
minutes ahead of `now`). A player who stops without `leave` just goes offline.

# Examples
```json
{"now":1727000000}
```
methods.returns_doc: Every player row with its `online` flag.

methods.name: heartbeat
methods.doc:
Report the caller's position and keep them online.

Send every 0.5 s while moving and every 2 s while idle; a player silent
for more than 10 s shows as offline. Creates the player row if needed.
Emits `PlayerJoined` only when this creates the row or brings a left
player back; otherwise no event.

# Examples
```json
{"t":{"name":"bot","x":64.5,"y":44.0,"z":64.5,"yaw":0.0,"pitch":0.0,"sel":0},"now":1727000000}
```

params.name: t
params.doc: position in blocks, `yaw` and `pitch` in radians, `sel` the hotbar slot (0 to 8).

methods.name: init
methods.doc:
Create the world. Runs once, when the context is created, with the
context's init arguments. The name, seed and creation time never change afterwards.

# Examples
```json
{"name":"ci","seed":42,"now":1727000000}
```

params.name: seed
params.doc: terrain seed; clients read it as an unsigned 32-bit integer, so use a value in [0, 4294967296).

params.name: now
params.doc: the creator's unix seconds; anchors the shared 600 s day/night cycle.

methods.name: join
methods.doc:
Join or rejoin the world as the calling identity and return the player row.

A new player starts at (0, 0, 0). A rejoin keeps the player's position and
join time and updates the name. `yaw`, `pitch` and `sel` reset to 0 either way.
Emits `PlayerJoined`.

# Examples
```json
{"name":"bot","now":1727000000}
```

params.name: name
params.doc: display name shown to other players.

methods.name: leave
methods.doc:
Mark the caller as having left. The row is kept, and a later `join` or
`heartbeat` brings the player back. A caller who never joined is a no-op.
Emits `PlayerLeft`.

# Examples
```json
{"now":1727000000}
```

methods.name: override_count
methods.doc:
How many distinct coordinates have ever been edited, breaks included.

# Examples
```json
{}
```
methods.returns_doc: The number of distinct coordinates ever edited.

methods.name: set_blocks
methods.doc:
Apply a batch of block edits and return how many were applied.

Out-of-bounds edits are skipped, not rejected, so one stale edit cannot
poison a batch. Each applied edit overwrites the block at its coordinate.
Emits `BlocksChanged` when at least one edit was applied.

# Errors
Fails, applying nothing, if more than 512 edits are sent in one call.

# Examples
```json
{"edits":[{"x":5,"y":20,"z":5,"b":3}],"now":1727000000}
```

params.name: edits
params.doc: at most 512 per call; `b` is a block id, 0 to 15 for ids the client defines (`b: 0` breaks the block); the contract stores any 0-255 value without checking it, so never send an id outside 0 to 15.

params.name: now
params.doc: the caller's unix seconds; orders concurrent edits of one block (last writer wins).

methods.returns_doc: How many edits were applied; skipped out-of-bounds edits are not counted.

methods.name: world_meta
methods.doc:
The world's name, terrain seed and creation time.

Terrain is not stored: regenerate it from `seed`, then apply `get_overrides`.

# Examples
```json
{}
```

events.name: BlocksChanged
events.doc: Blocks were edited; the payload is the editor's identity. Re-read `get_overrides`.

events.name: PlayerJoined
events.doc: A player joined or came back; the payload is their identity.

events.name: PlayerLeft
events.doc: A player called `leave`; the payload is their identity.
